name: run-I/run-J
purpose: the train/val/test assignment both the Run I (W32 shortlist teacher) and Run J (production mc-s0-report-lcb teacher) corpora bind to. They deal the identical 16,000 deals, so one assignment governs both and the I-minus-J contrast cannot be knocked out of alignment by the split.
derivation: deal_key(deck_from_seed(round_mix_draw(round_mix, seed0, c))) for c in range(clusters), then split_deals(keys, seed=split_seed, val_fraction, test_fraction). A pure function of the fields above: no shard is read and no card is played, so the assignment is knowable before either run finishes.
keys_sha256_recipe: sha256 of the 16,000 deal keys in cluster order, newline-joined, no trailing newline
assignment_sha256_recipe: sha256 of '<deal_key> <part>' lines in cluster order, newline-joined, no trailing newline

independent_replication.result: 16,000 deals, identical key set, zero differing assignments

verified_against_shards.note: enumerated keys compared to the deck of the first record of every shard each run had written at the time

chosen_before_results_note: split_seed 7 was fixed while neither corpus had trained anything and no I or J outcome had been read, so the holdouts are holdouts. Anyone changing it after a result exists is choosing a split to fit an answer.
